label: A/B compartment analysis
definition: Classify megabase-scale genomic regions into transcriptionally active (A) or inactive (B) compartments based on the principal eigenvector of a chromatin contact matrix from Hi-C or Micro-C data.

label: Admixture analysis
definition: Quantify the proportion of ancestry from distinct source populations in admixed individuals using genome-wide variant data.

label: Alpha diversity analysis
definition: Quantify species richness and evenness within a single microbial community sample using metrics such as Shannon entropy, observed species count, or Faith's phylogenetic diversity.

label: Ambient RNA correction
definition: Estimate and remove background RNA contamination arising from lysed cells that contaminates droplet-based single-cell libraries, using methods such as SoupX or DecontX.

label: Amplicon sequence analysis
definition: End-to-end processing of marker-gene amplicon sequencing data (16S rRNA, 18S rRNA, ITS), including primer trimming, quality filtering, denoising, and taxonomic assignment.

label: Batch effect correction
definition: Remove unwanted technical variation attributable to experimental batch, platform, reagent lot, or processing date from molecular data while preserving biological signal.

label: Beta diversity analysis
definition: Compare the microbial community composition between samples using ecological distance or dissimilarity metrics such as UniFrac, Bray-Curtis, or Jaccard distance.

label: Biological sequence embedding
definition: Generate dense continuous vector representations of biological sequences using a trained language model or encoder such as ESM-2, ProtTrans, Nucleotide Transformer, or DNABERT.

label: Cell barcode correction
definition: Identify and correct sequencing errors in cell barcodes from droplet-based single-cell sequencing experiments to accurately assign reads to their cell of origin.

label: Cell-cell communication analysis
definition: Infer intercellular signaling interactions by identifying co-expression of ligand-receptor gene pairs across cell populations from single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data.

label: Cell clustering
definition: Group individual cells into discrete clusters based on similarity of their molecular profiles, typically using graph-based community detection algorithms applied to a k-nearest neighbor graph of cell embeddings.

label: Cell type annotation
definition: Assign biological cell type identities to cells or cell clusters using marker gene expression patterns, reference transcriptome atlases, or automated label-transfer classifiers.

label: Cell type deconvolution
definition: Estimate the proportional composition of distinct cell types within bulk tissue samples by reference to a single-cell or cell-type-specific expression signature dataset.

label: Chromatin accessibility analysis
definition: Quantify open chromatin regions genome-wide from ATAC-seq or DNase-seq data, including read alignment, peak calling, nucleosome positioning, and per-locus accessibility scoring.

label: Chromatin conformation analysis
definition: Process and analyze data from chromosome conformation capture experiments (Hi-C, Micro-C, 4C, ChIA-PET) to characterize the spatial organization of the genome in the nucleus.

label: Chromatin loop calling
definition: Detect focal point-to-point long-range chromatin interactions (loops) between pairs of genomic loci from Hi-C or ChIA-PET contact maps.

label: Chromatin organization analysis
definition: Analysis of the three-dimensional organization of chromatin in the nucleus, including higher-order genome folding, chromatin accessibility, and long-range regulatory interactions.

label: Contact matrix normalization
definition: Correct systematic biases in chromatin contact matrices from Hi-C experiments including distance-dependent decay, GC content bias, and mappability, using methods such as ICE, KR, or VC normalization.

label: CRISPR off-target prediction
definition: Computationally identify and score genomic loci susceptible to unintended nuclease cleavage based on sequence similarity to a CRISPR guide RNA, to inform guide design or experimental validation priorities.

label: CRISPR screen analysis
definition: Identify genes that affect a phenotype or cellular fitness by measuring changes in guide RNA abundance across time points or conditions in a pooled CRISPR knockout or activation library screen.

label: Demographic modeling
definition: Infer historical population size changes, divergence times, and migration rates from site frequency spectra or other population genetic summary statistics.

label: Direct RNA base modification detection
definition: Call RNA base modifications (m6A, pseudouridine, inosine) directly from nanopore ionic current signal without chemical conversion, using signal-level models trained on characteristic disruption patterns.

label: Doublet/multiplet detection
definition: Identify cell barcodes in single-cell sequencing data that represent the co-encapsulation and co-sequencing of two or more cells rather than a single cell.

label: Full-length isoform analysis
definition: Characterize complete transcript isoforms, including alternative splicing events and novel transcripts, from full-length long-read cDNA or direct RNA sequencing data.

label: Functional genomics analysis
definition: Large-scale analysis of the functional consequences of genomic elements or variants, encompassing CRISPR screens, massively parallel reporter assays, saturation genome editing, and related systematic perturbation experiments.

label: Functional metagenomic prediction
definition: Infer the functional gene content and metabolic pathway potential of a microbial community from its taxonomic composition or from direct annotation of metagenomic sequences.

label: Gene fusion detection
definition: Identify chimeric transcripts arising from chromosomal rearrangements, read-through transcription, or trans-splicing from RNA-seq data, or gene-fusing structural variants from whole-genome sequencing.

label: Genome editing analysis
definition: Design and computational analysis of experiments that use programmable nucleases (CRISPR-Cas, TALENs, zinc finger nucleases) to introduce targeted modifications to genomic DNA.

label: Genome editing outcome analysis
definition: Quantify the spectrum of insertion, deletion, and precise editing outcomes at a CRISPR target locus from amplicon sequencing data, including indel frequency, allele enumeration, and repair template incorporation rate.

label: Genome-wide association analysis
definition: Test statistical associations between genetic variants across the genome and a phenotypic trait in large cohorts to identify loci that influence the trait.

label: Guide RNA design
definition: Design and score candidate guide RNA sequences (sgRNA or crRNA) for CRISPR-based genome editing, optimizing for on-target activity efficacy and specificity against off-target genomic loci.

label: Haplotype-resolved assembly
definition: Produce a phased genome assembly in which each haplotype of a diploid or polyploid organism is represented as a separate contiguous sequence, using long reads, Hi-C scaffolding, or parental trio information.

label: Hyperparameter optimization
definition: Systematically search the configuration space of a machine learning model to identify hyperparameter settings that maximize held-out predictive performance, using strategies such as grid search, random search, or Bayesian optimization.

label: Long-read assembly polishing
definition: Iteratively correct systematic sequence errors in a draft genome or transcriptome assembly using additional sequencing reads, reducing indel and substitution error rates in the final assembly.

label: Machine learning
definition: Computational methods that train, evaluate, or apply statistical models learned from data, encompassing classical machine learning algorithms and deep learning approaches applied to biological data.

label: Machine learning model training
definition: Fit a machine learning or deep learning model to a labeled or unlabeled training dataset by minimizing a loss function, yielding a parameterized model applicable to new data.

label: Metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) analysis
definition: Recover, assess quality (completeness and contamination), and taxonomically classify genome bins assembled from shotgun metagenomic sequencing data.

label: Microbial differential abundance analysis
definition: Identify microbial taxa that are significantly differentially abundant between experimental conditions using statistical models that account for the compositional nature of relative abundance data.

label: Microbiome analysis
definition: Analysis of microbial community composition and function from metagenomic or marker-gene amplicon sequencing data.

label: Model cross-validation and evaluation
definition: Assess the predictive performance of a machine learning model on held-out data using k-fold, leave-one-out, or other cross-validation procedures, reporting metrics appropriate to the task such as AUC, F1, precision-recall, or RMSE.

label: Multi-omics analysis
definition: Integrated analysis of two or more distinct molecular measurement modalities (omics layers) from the same biological samples to identify coordinated patterns of variation across data types.

label: Multi-omics data integration
definition: Combine and jointly analyze heterogeneous molecular datasets from two or more omics layers measured in the same samples using latent variable, network, or matrix factorization approaches.

label: Multi-omics factor analysis
definition: Decompose multi-omics datasets into shared and dataset-specific latent factors capturing coordinated sources of biological variation across omics layers, using methods such as MOFA+ or JIVE.

label: Neural network inference
definition: Apply a trained neural network model to new input data to generate predictions, classifications, or embeddings without updating the model parameters.

label: OTU/ASV generation
definition: Cluster amplicon sequencing reads into operational taxonomic units (OTUs) or denoise them into exact amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) to represent distinct microbial taxa.

label: Polygenic score calculation
definition: Aggregate the per-allele effects of many genetic variants distributed across the genome into a single score predicting an individual's genetic predisposition to a quantitative or disease trait.

label: Population differentiation calculation
definition: Calculate allele frequency-based statistics that quantify genetic differentiation between two or more populations, such as FST, PBS, or related measures.

label: Population genetics analysis
definition: Statistical analysis of genetic variation across populations of individuals to infer demographic history, population structure, selection pressures, and genotype-phenotype associations.

label: Population structure analysis
definition: Infer the number of ancestral populations and assign individuals to population clusters from genome-wide variant data, using methods such as STRUCTURE, ADMIXTURE, or principal component analysis.

label: RNA velocity analysis
definition: Estimate the future transcriptional state of individual cells by modeling RNA splicing kinetics from the ratio of unspliced to spliced transcript abundances, as a proxy for transcriptional activity.

label: Runs of homozygosity analysis
definition: Detect extended genomic segments of continuous homozygosity (ROH) indicative of inbreeding, autozygosity, or recent positive selection sweeps.

label: Selective sweep analysis
definition: Detect genomic signatures of recent positive selection using haplotype-based statistics such as iHS or XP-EHH, nucleotide diversity scans, or allele frequency-based methods such as Tajima's D.

label: Single-cell analysis
definition: Analysis of data derived from single-cell sequencing or profiling experiments, in which molecular measurements are made at the resolution of individual cells.

label: Single-cell data integration
definition: Harmonize single-cell datasets from different batches, donors, technologies, or modalities into a common embedding that removes technical variation while preserving biological variation.

label: Single-cell multiomics analysis
definition: Jointly analyze two or more molecular modalities measured simultaneously in the same individual cells, such as gene expression and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) or surface protein abundance (CITE-seq).

label: Spatial domain identification
definition: Partition a tissue section from a spatially resolved transcriptomics experiment into spatially coherent regions with distinct molecular signatures, analogous to histological tissue segmentation.

label: Spatial gene expression analysis
definition: Process and analyze spatially resolved transcriptomic data to link gene expression measurements to their physical coordinates within a tissue section.

label: Spatial neighborhood analysis
definition: Characterize the molecular composition and cell type enrichment of the local cellular microenvironment surrounding each spot or cell in a spatially resolved transcriptomic dataset.

label: Spatial omics analysis
definition: Analysis of molecular profiling data that retains the spatial coordinates of measurements within a tissue section or biological specimen, including spatially resolved transcriptomics and proteomics.

label: Spatial spot/cell deconvolution
definition: Estimate the cell type composition of each spatial capture unit (spot or segmented cell) in a spatially resolved transcriptomics experiment using a single-cell reference expression atlas.

label: Spatially variable gene detection
definition: Identify genes whose expression varies significantly across tissue space in a spatially resolved transcriptomics dataset, beyond variation attributable to chance or differences in cell type composition.

label: Topologically associating domain (TAD) identification
definition: Partition the genome into contiguous self-interacting chromatin domains (topologically associating domains, TADs) separated by boundary regions of reduced Hi-C contact frequency.

label: Trajectory inference
definition: Order cells along a continuous path or branching graph representing a biological process such as differentiation, reprogramming, or the cell cycle, inferring pseudotemporal progression from single-cell expression data.

label: Transcription factor footprinting
definition: Identify transcription factor occupancy events from characteristic protection patterns within ATAC-seq or DNase-seq chromatin accessibility data.

label: Transfer learning
definition: Adapt a machine learning model pre-trained on large biological datasets to a new prediction task or organism by continued training on a smaller, task-specific dataset.

label: UMI deduplication
definition: Remove PCR duplicate reads in single-cell sequencing data by collapsing reads with identical cell barcodes and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) to a single molecule count.
